context: Decide first whether a username is a secret to redact or an identifier to pseudonymize - the anonymization path already treats it as the latter, and treating one channel as secret while the other pseudonymizes is a policy split worth making deliberately rather than by default. If redaction is chosen, guard over-redaction as #1346 did: a bare 'user' substring also matches user_agent and num_users, so prefer bounded matching plus a non-credential guard test. Once shared handling covers it, DuckLake's adapter-local _CREDENTIAL_CONFIG_KEYS scrub can shrink.
description: is_secret_option_key() (platform_options.py:72) does not match user/username/pg_user/http_user/login/account, so any adapter carrying a username in platform_config exports it verbatim in platform_raw_config. Measured 2026-07-31 on develop 8c9d7f8d8: sanitize_platform_options({'username':'alice-sentinel'}) returns it unchanged, and PostgreSQLAdapter(username=...,password=...) normalized metadata carries username in clear while password is '<redacted>'. Affects the ~25 adapters holding credential config. CORRECTION vs the first draft of this item, which rated this high and claimed published results were affected: the PUBLIC anonymization path PSEUDONYMIZES usernames (alice-sentinel -> user_b860e7bd6314) via identifier_keys, so published results are NOT exposed. The exposure is limited to internal/unanonymized result metadata - real, but a narrower channel than first claimed, hence medium. PR #1364 fixed this for DuckLake only via an adapter-local key scrub.

preserves.behavior: Non-credential keys such as user_agent still export real values
Public/anonymized export keeps pseudonymizing usernames rather than redacting them, unless w1 deliberately changes that
